analysis: The only supplied change is docs/developer/build.md. The base excerpt covers lines 935-1246 and the head excerpt covers lines 1-446. The head excerpt does not include the surrounding App Attest sections, so the two sides are not directly comparable. No executable code, workflow, authorization, encryption, billing or attestation logic changed in the supplied units. Relevant threat IDs are TB-011, T-053, T-054, T-052, T-057, T-041 and A-017. The head text restates the build and release-publication behavior at lines 257-263. Publication stages an immutable digest path and then registers the exact official build via the scoped POST /v1/releases. It makes no per-release hardware qualification or manual approval requirement. This is consistent with the canonical context, which states that final signed-artifact and physical-transition validation concerns activation of serving or removal policy, not a per-release publication gate. Secret-bearing jobs accept verified signed annotated production tags in reviewed master ancestry, or trusted master for dev, manual and recovery runs, and the docs assume trusted repository writers. This is a documented assumption, not a new gap. Release-plumbing PRs run with PR-scoped caches and no signing or publishing secrets (lines 366-373). Cache descriptions say that restored runtime bundles and metallibs are discarded and that signing keys are never cached. I could not verify the actual workflow or scripts, so a deeper pass should check them if they change elsewhere in the PR. No security regression is evident from documentation alone.
